transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today, I really appreciate it. Um... I guess I'm here because... well, I've just been feeling a little stuck lately. I'm sorry, I don't want to sound overly dramatic right off the bat, but... I just can't seem to shake this really heavy, hopeless feeling. 

It kind of feels like everything I tried to build after my divorce has just... collapsed. And I'm just sort of sitting under it, if that makes sense? I know that's probably a lot to drop on you in the first five minutes, I'm sorry. Am I explaining this okay?
How long have you been feeling this heavy, hopeless feeling?

Um... I'd say it's been about a month? Give or take. It really started to, um, hang over me right around the time I was dealing with all the financial... well, the financial mess after the divorce. I mean, I know everyone gets stressed about money and breakups, so I really try not to complain too much, and I'm sure it's probably a normal reaction... but it just hasn't lifted since then. Is that a normal timeframe for something like this? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you lost interest in activities that you normally enjoy?

Um... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I still try to keep up with things, you know? I don't want to just sit around and do nothing. But... well, I used to love reading, and lately I just can't seem to focus on a book. And I haven't really felt like going out with my friends as much. 

But I'm sure that's just because I've been so tired with everything going on, right? It's not like I've completely stopped doing everything. I still go to work and everything. Does that sound like what you mean by losing interest, or am I misunderstanding the question?
Have you noticed any changes in your weight recently?

Um... no, not really. I mean, my clothes still fit the same, mostly. I guess maybe I haven't been cooking as much as I usually do, but I'm still eating, you know? Just... maybe simpler things, or whatever is easy to grab. 

I haven't noticed any major changes on the scale or anything like that. I try to make sure I'm still taking care of myself in that way, so I don't think there's anything to worry about there. Is that what you were looking for? I hope that's helpful.
Have you been having any trouble sleeping?

Um... well, maybe a little bit? I mean, I know everyone has a bad night here and there, especially with stress, so I don't want to make a big deal out of it. But... lately, I guess I do kind of lie awake sometimes, just staring at the ceiling. My mind just keeps replaying all the bills and, you know, little mistakes I made at work. 

And then sometimes I'll wake up way before dawn, and it just feels like I never actually slept at all. But I'm sure that's just my body adjusting to everything, right? I try really hard to stick to a normal bedtime so I'm well-rested for work. Does that sound like the kind of trouble sleeping you mean, or is that just normal stress?
Have you had any thoughts of death or suicide?

Um... well, I know everyone gets overwhelmed sometimes, and I really don't want to sound dramatic or anything. I mean, I know I have a lot to be thankful for. But... I guess things have just felt so heavy lately. 

I haven't, like, made any actual plans or anything like that. I would never want to do that to my family. But... sometimes I've just been thinking that maybe it would be easier if I just... didn't wake up? Just to get a break from everything. It's just a passing thought, mostly. But... well, to be honest, a few days ago the thoughts got a little more intense, and it actually scared me a bit. I didn't want to bother anyone I know, so I ended up calling the employee assistance program at work, just to talk to someone. 

I'm really trying my best to handle everything, I promise. I know it's not a good way to think. Is it okay that I told you that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you had any difficulty concentrating on things like work or daily tasks?

Um... well, I really try to stay on top of my work, you know? I don't want to let my team down or anything. But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, things have been taking me a little longer lately. 

It's just silly things, really. Like, I'll look at a basic drainage calculation, or a spreadsheet that I've literally used for years, and my mind just kind of... blanks. I just sit there rereading the same numbers over and over, and I can't seem to trust myself to make a decision on it. It's so frustrating because I know how to do it. I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job, so I end up double and triple-checking everything, which slows me down. 

I'm sure it's just because I'm a little tired, right? I really hope it's not affecting my performance too much. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your questions right.
Have you felt worthless or guilty about things you've done or haven't done?

Um... I mean, I know I shouldn't be so hard on myself. Everyone makes mistakes, right? And I really try to be positive and do my best for everyone. But... lately, I just... I can't seem to stop feeling like I'm just... messing everything up. 

I keep telling myself that I'm a terrible engineer, and honestly, a failed wife, too. It just feels like I'm this huge burden to the people around me. I know it's probably just my mind playing tricks on me, but I keep replaying every little missed calculation at work, or every tense email I've sent... and it just feels like absolute proof that I ruin things. 

I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself, though. I really do try to push past it. It's just hard to ignore sometimes. Is it normal to get stuck on things like that when you're stressed out? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the full picture.
Have you been experiencing these feelings of worthlessness and guilt nearly every day?

Um... yeah, I suppose so. I really hate to sound like I'm just complaining, because I know everyone has their own problems to deal with and I should be able to handle mine. But... yes, pretty much every day. 

It's been... well, this whole heavy feeling has been hanging over me for about a month now. I think it all kind of started... um... I'm a little embarrassed to even admit this, because I feel like I should be more put together at my age, but... it started around this awful financial mess I had to sort out. Right after my divorce. 

I really try to keep my personal life from affecting me this much, I promise. I always try to put on a brave face for everyone. I just haven't been able to shake it off this time. I hope I'm giving you the right details... is that the kind of timeline you were asking about?
Have you experienced a significant loss of pleasure in most activities for most of the day?

Um... well, I really do try to stay active and keep up with my hobbies, you know? I think it's important to have a good work-life balance and not just sit around. I still force myself to go to my book club and take my dog for his walks because I want to be responsible.

But... I guess if I'm thinking about it... I wouldn't say I've completely lost pleasure in things. It's more just that... it takes a lot more effort to get myself to do them? Like, I'll be at book club, and everyone is laughing and talking, and I'm smiling and nodding along so I don't bring the mood down, but inside I just kind of feel... flat. Like I'm just going through the motions. 

I still love my dog, of course, and I love my friends. I just don't get that same spark of joy from seeing them right now. I'm sure it's just the stress catching up with me, and I'll bounce back soon. Does that make sense? I hope that answers your question okay.
Have you had more than two weeks where you felt this heavy, hopeless feeling nearly every day?

Um... yes, definitely more than two weeks. I know I mentioned it just a little bit ago, and I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, but... yeah, it's been about a month now that this whole heavy feeling has just been hanging over me. 

I really wish I could say I snapped out of it faster. I know I should be stronger than this. But it just hasn't lifted since... well, since that financial mess started right after the divorce. I've really been trying to push through it and not let it get the best of me, I promise. I just... I haven't been able to shake it for the past month. Is that the kind of timeframe you needed to know about? I want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or the opposite, feeling restless and fidgety?

Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I really try to stay on top of things and keep my energy up, especially at work. As an engineer, I can't really afford to be slow or miss details, you know? So I make sure I'm always moving at my normal pace. 

And as for being restless... well, maybe I fidget a tiny bit sometimes if I'm trying to focus on a tough project, but nothing out of the ordinary. I'm definitely not pacing around or anything disruptive like that. I always try to be mindful of how I'm coming across to others. I hope that's what you were asking? I haven't really noticed any big changes in how I move or talk.
Have you experienced any psychomotor agitation or retardation nearly every day?

Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I think you just asked me something similar, right? About moving slow or being restless? I hope I didn't misunderstand the last question, I really want to give you the right answers. 

But no, I haven't noticed anything like that. I'm pretty steady, really. I try to keep myself composed, especially because I don't want people at work or my friends to think I'm... well, acting strange or anything. I just go about my day normally, maybe a little more tired, but my movements and everything are fine. Does that make sense? I hope that's helpful.
Have you experienced significant impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning nearly every day?

Um... well... I guess things have been a bit harder lately. I mean, I really, really try to keep it all together, especially at work. I know how important my job is, and I hate letting anyone down. But... um... I guess I was making some... questionable calls on a few projects. I just couldn't think straight, and I ended up getting really overwhelmed and kind of falling apart during a few meetings. I was so embarrassed. My supervisor actually had to take me off making active project decisions for a bit. I felt awful about it, I really did. I'm usually so much more reliable than that.

And at home... well, I haven't been keeping up with things the way I should. Just basic routines, you know? It's embarrassing to admit. And... um... it actually got bad enough that I ended up having to go to the emergency department. I just... I didn't feel safe with my own thoughts, and I didn't know what else to do. I hope you don't think less of me for that. I'm really trying to get back on track and be the person I'm supposed to be. Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Have you experienced a lack of reactivity to normally pleasurable stimuli nearly every day?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I still try to enjoy the things I usually do. Like, I'll still put on a movie or try to read a little bit, because I know that's what I'm supposed to do to relax, right? I want to make sure I'm doing the right things to take care of myself. 

So, yeah, if something good happens, I think I still react to it. I always try to show appreciation when people do nice things for me, or smile if someone tells a joke. I really don't want to bring anyone else down or seem ungrateful. I hope that makes sense? I'm trying my best to stay positive and appreciate the good things, I really am.
Have you experienced a depressive episode that has lasted for more than two months?

Um... well, no, not two months. It hasn't been that long, I promise. I've really been trying not to let it drag on, because I know I need to get back to normal. 

It's been... about a month, I think? Ever since... um, well, my divorce got finalized, and there was this whole financial mess that came with it. I tried so hard to handle it all gracefully, I really did, but it just sort of... started hanging over me after that. I've been doing everything I can to shake it off, though. I hope that's okay? I just didn't want you to think I've been stuck like this forever. I'm really working on it.
Have you experienced any episodes of depression that have lasted less than two months but are still significantly impacting your daily life?

Um... yes, I think that's exactly it. Like I mentioned, it hasn't been two months, but... it's definitely been impacting me. It's been about a month now, just... sort of hanging over me. 

It all really started right around when the divorce was finalized and... well, all that financial mess happened. I really thought I could just push through it and handle it without letting it affect my life so much. I've been trying so hard to keep up with everything and not let it drag me down, but it's just been a bit harder than I expected to bounce back. I hope you understand? I'm really trying my best to get past it so I can get back to being myself.
Have you found it difficult to make decisions on a daily basis due to your current state of mind?

Um... well, maybe a little bit? I mean, I try really hard to stay on top of things, especially at work. I don't want anyone to think I'm slacking off or that I can't do my job. But... lately, I guess it has been a bit harder to just... make a call on things. 

Like, I'll be looking at a basic drainage calculation, or a spreadsheet I've used for years as a civil engineer, and my mind just sort of... blanks? I end up sitting there, rereading the same numbers over and over, and I just can't seem to trust myself to make the right decision. I know I should be able to do it easily, and I really am trying to push through it. I just... I don't want to make a mistake and cause problems for anyone else. Does that make sense? I'm hoping it's just a temporary thing and I'll be back to my normal self soon.
Do you feel that your current depressive feelings are mildly, moderately, or severely impacting your daily life?

Um... I guess... I guess it might be on the more severe side? I mean, I really didn't want it to get this bad, and I tried so hard to keep it together. But... well, I was making some questionable calls at work, and I kind of started falling apart in meetings. My supervisor actually had to take me off active project decisions. I felt so terrible about letting the team down, I really did. 

And at home... I just stopped keeping up with basic routines. It got to the point where... um, I actually ended up being sent to the emergency department because... well, I just didn't feel safe with my own thoughts anymore. I'm so sorry, I know that sounds awful, and I really am trying to get better. I just... I hope you don't think less of me for letting things get this far out of hand. I'm doing my best to fix it, I promise. Is it okay that I told you that?
